prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Wildmere; priority safety>protection>export. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss, shutdown on confirmed fire; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System (safe blade position on emergency shutdown), Rotor Brake Unit (per protection sequence), Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor (fault vs fire info)→Turbine Sensor Bus. Mode Turbine Lockout: no remote restart during fire investigation/post-event checks. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer (site-specific trips), export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel (alarms with location/fault), fire detection coordinated with isolation; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment; mode Substation Degraded. Alarm priorities separate danger vs supervisory faults; not cleared just because detector normal. Substation Operator switches only in active window with Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Outages: Marine Coordinator checks vessel timing; Electrical Technician confirms scope, inspects only after safe assessment and isolations; Work Permit Portal updated before start; unsafe→pause; Duty Planner records times. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, load priorities, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry/alarms→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay), not replacing local controls; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room assesses alarms, initiates response; keeps last validated limit on comms loss. Control Engineer verifies protection complete before further action; reviews alarms with SCADA Engineer. Operations Radio Console: voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft, response instructions; Vessel Master read-back, holds position for recovery; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. Evacuation: muster; Personnel Tracking Console accountability; HSE Officer advises re-entry; Field Supervisor reports work party status→Shore Control Room. North Access Scanner validates readable, identifiable credentials. Comms: authorized channels, fallback, urgent messages state asset/hazard/action/issuer. Records: synced clocks, corrections preserve original; Cybersecurity Analyst protects logs; legal holds. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag.

New part:
S812: The person presents the credential at the controlled entry point and waits for the scanner response.
S813: The scanner checks that the authorization is active for the scheduled work period.
S814: It also checks that the requested access area is within the person's approved scope.
S815: An authorization that is expired, suspended, or incomplete results in a denied entry decision.
S816: The gate remains secured when the scanner cannot verify a credential or retrieve the required authorization information.
S817: A denial directs the person to contact the Field Supervisor or the HSE Officer for review.
S818: Neither a verbal request nor a manually presented credential image overrides a scanner denial.
S819: Approved entry is granted only after all configured identity and authorization checks pass.
S820: Each attempt receives a unique transaction identifier for later reference.
S821: The transaction records the credential identifier, decision time, access point, and decision outcome.
S822: It also records the authorization version and the rule that determined the outcome.
S823: The audit record distinguishes a rejected credential from an authorization that lacks the required scope.
S824: The system retains successful and unsuccessful attempts under the site's access record retention policy.
S825: Access records are protected against unauthorized alteration and are available to authorized reviewers.
S826: The Field Supervisor reviews unusual denial patterns and unresolved access exceptions during the work shift.
S827: The HSE Officer can use the recorded entry history to support personnel accountability during an incident.
S828: If the scanner is unavailable, personnel follow the approved contingency process rather than bypassing the gate.
S829: The contingency process requires a named approver and a recorded reason for any temporary access decision.
S830: Temporary decisions are reconciled against the normal access record when scanner service is restored.
S831: The scanner displays a clear outcome without exposing unnecessary personal information to people nearby.
S832: Operators verify the scanner clock and connectivity during routine readiness checks.
S833: Changes to access rules are controlled and reviewed before they become effective at the entry point.
S834: This control provides a consistent basis for admitting authorized personnel and explaining each access decision.
S835: South Access Scanner serves the designated southern entry route to the offshore wind farm.
S836: The route is intended for personnel arriving through the south-side access point.
S837: Its location and operating hours are defined in the site access plan.
S838: The scanner applies the same identity verification standard used at other controlled entry points.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
